title: Badge
docs:
## Installation **Command** ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/badge ``` **Manual** Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI. 1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed. ```package-manager npm install clsx tailwind-merge @base-ui/react class-variance-authority ``` 2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers. - [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency. 3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines. | Item | Target file | Full source | | --- | --- | --- | | cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) | | badge | `@components/cadence/badge/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/badge.json) | [Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) [Source files: badge](https://cadence.dev/r/badge.json) 4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition. No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme. Badge needs only the files and packages listed above; no motion runtime, provider or additional item-specific CSS is required. The With an icon example also uses `lucide-react`. Install it only when using those icons; Badge itself does not require an icon package: ```package-manager npm install lucide-react ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Badge } from "@/components/cadence/badge"; export function Release() { return (
Parity plan 0.2.0
); } ``` ## Variants Choose one of six visual weights for a status or category. The `link` variant is only a style; use `render` when the badge should navigate. ```tsx import { Badge } from "@/components/cadence/badge"; export function BadgeVariants() { return (
Default Secondary Destructive Outline Ghost Link
); } ``` ## With an icon Pair a short label with an icon; the text still communicates the status without depending on the icon or colour. ```tsx import { CheckIcon, ClockIcon, GitBranchIcon } from "lucide-react"; import { Badge } from "@/components/cadence/badge"; export function BadgeIcons() { return (
Verified Pending main
); } ``` ## As a link `render` replaces the element, so a badge stays a `span` unless you ask for something else. The `[a&]` selectors only switch on hover when it really is a link. These anchors use native focus and Enter navigation to the changelog. ```tsx import { Badge } from "@/components/cadence/badge"; export function BadgeLinks() { return (
}>3 releases }>Changelog
); } ``` ## When to use - A short status: `Active`, `Beta`, `Deprecated`, `3 open`. - A category or tag next to a title, where the colour carries the grouping. - A count attached to a navigation item or a filter chip. ## When not to use - Anything the user must click to act; use `button` (a badge has no focus, no press feedback, and no keyboard path). - More than about three words. A long label belongs in running text or in a `card` header, not in a pill. - A status that changes while the user watches; use `toast` or an inline message, because a badge swap is easy to miss. ## API | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------ | | `variant` | `"default" \| "secondary" \| "outline" \| "ghost" \| "destructive" \| "link"` | `"default"` | Visual weight. | | `render` | `ReactElement \| (props, state) => ReactElement` | – | Base UI composition; replaces `asChild`. | | `className` | `string` | – | Merged last. | `data-slot="badge"` and `data-variant` are rendered from the component's state, so you can restyle per variant from CSS without touching this file. All native span props are forwarded. ## Motion contract No motion (T0). A badge labels content; it does not enter, leave, or move. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ----------------------------------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | `transition-[color,box-shadow]` is state feedback on the design tokens (hover on a linked badge, the focus ring), not motion: it never moves the box and never runs on mount. ## Accessibility - The badge is a `span`, so it is not in the tab order and has no role — the text itself is the message. - Colour is never the only signal: every variant still carries readable text. - When rendered as a link it inherits the anchor's semantics, focus ring, and keyboard behaviour, and gains `[a&]:hover` styles automatically. ## Responsiveness and performance Badges keep intrinsic width and do not wrap their text. Keep labels short; let the parent wrap a collection or provide an overflow strategy for long labels. T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. Base UI behavior requires hydration; native HTML behavior remains browser-owned. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately. ## Notes for AI - Never attach `onClick` to a badge; switch to `button` with `size="sm"`. - Do not animate a badge in or out. If the status changes, swap the text and let `aria-live` on the surrounding region announce it.
